relation_semantics.taughtIn: The subject concept/skill is actually introduced or covered in the named object lecture, not merely tangentially related to it.
relation_semantics.prerequisiteOf: The subject must be understood before the object can be reasonably understood or performed — a prerequisite edge in a teaching sequence.
relation_semantics.dependsOn: The subject cannot be reasonably understood without the object already having been learned.
relation_semantics.contrastsWith: The subject and object are alternative approaches to the same kind of problem that a student needs to actively learn to distinguish or choose between.
relation_semantics.usesConcept: Performing or explaining the subject genuinely requires knowledge of the object concept — load-bearing, not incidental.
relation_semantics.operatesOnType: The subject construct commonly and directly operates on values of the object data type.
relation_semantics.producesType: Evaluating or calling the subject construct/method actually yields a value of the object type.
relation_semantics.acceptsType: The subject construct accepts a value of the object type as one of its inputs.
relation_semantics.methodOf: The subject method is genuinely defined on/callable on values of the object type.
relation_semantics.throwsError: Using the subject construct/concept can, under realistic conditions, actually raise the named object error.
relation_semantics.exampleOf: The subject is a concrete worked example that illustrates the object concept.
relation_semantics.implementedBy: The subject skill/concept is concretely realized by the object language construct in this course's material.
relation_semantics.timeComplexity: The subject algorithm's cost is genuinely characterized by the object complexity concept as taught in this course.
relation_semantics.solvesProblem: The subject skill is the applicable technique for addressing the object problem/concept.
relation_semantics.bestPractice: The object is a recommended practice genuinely associated with applying the subject skill/concept.
